newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - Heating oil demand slows stocks build-up.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Heating oil demand slows stocks build-up.

text.p: Strong U.S. heating oil demand slowed a seasonal build-up of inventories as refiners worked to cut into a shortfall in stocks ahead of the winter heating season, analysts said on Tuesday.

Heating oil stocks rose 1.57 million barrels in the East Coast region but remained more than 14 million barrels below last year's levels, the American Petroleum Institute said in its weekly petroleum products survey.
"The demand side was quite firm," said Steven Platt, a Deam Witter energy analyst based in Chicago.
"I'm looking for this demand to come off, and it has not as of yet," Platt said.

Analysts surveyed by Reuters had expected distillate inventories, fueled by higher heating oil output, to rise by 2.5 million barrels last week. Instead, distillate inventories on hand fell a modest 429,000 barrels to end the week at 117.46 million barrels nationwide, said API, a Washington, D.C.-based trade group.
Refineries were operating at a blistering 93.9 percent of capacity, down 0.1 percentage point from the prior week but 4.4 percentage points above the same week last year, API said.
API said crude oil stocks surged last week, rising a net 9.3 million barrels as Gulf Coast and West Coast refiners added significantly to inventories.
But analysts said the build, which left crude stocks nationwide at 312.4 million barrels, may be overstated based on the trade group's estimates of crude oil production, imports and crude runs.
Crude imports fell to an average 7.04 million barrels per day while domestic production was unchanged at 6.4 million barrels per day and crude runs rose a modest 37,000 barrels per day, API said.
"The crude stocks appear overstated, particularly on the West Coast," a Midwest analyst said, adding the API estimates may not fully account for crude exports from the West Coast.

Based on the API figures, analysts estimated each barrel of crude oil was yielding an average 24.9 percent distillates and 53.1 percent gasoline, a slight drop in distillate output compared to the prior week.

Gasoline inventories nationwide stood at 190.76 million barrels, rising a net 4.74 million barrels. The build was driven largely by a 2.8 million barrel increase in gasoline stocks held in primary storage by East Coast refineries.
NYMEX December heating oil was bid 66.00 cents a gallon, asked 66.15 cents in ACCESS after-hours trade, firming after settling off 0.53 cent at 65.42 cents in the floor session.
December gasoline was bid 64.26 cents a gallon, asked 64.45 cents after settling down 0.39 cent at 64.61 cents.
December crude oil was asked $22.67 a barrel in after-hours trade with no bids after closing 15 cents lower at $22.64 a barrel.
